clue.text: Cool quality of most aircraft wings?

definitions.text: Cool quality of most aircraft wings?

parts.words: Cool quality of most aircraft wings?
parts.note: unlike a bird's, an aeroplane's wings stay rigid and never beat up and down, so they show the composure the clue calls cool

explanation.surface: A question about what quality the wings of most aircraft share.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means calmness under pressure, but read literally it is the inability of fixed wings to beat like a bird's.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure in a crisis is what 'cool' means here, the state of never getting flustered.

clue.text: Mum's curry — poetry on occasion, one assumes!

indicators.note: only now and then, so just every other letter of these words is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Mum's cooking is compared, now and then, to poetry, as one might suppose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on occasion' takes the even letters of MUMS CURRY POETRY. 'One assumes' means someone who assumes power or a throne, not someone supposing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender seizes a throne or office that is not theirs, assuming power without right.

clue.text: Right to be utterly liberated?

parts.note: 'utterly' is read as 'in uttering', so the right is to be liberated in what one says

explanation.surface: A question about whether one has the right to be completely free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like 'completely' but is read as 'in what is uttered'.
explanation.definitionFit: This civil liberty protects people's right to voice opinions without censorship.

clue.text: A majority of capital raised in addition

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters turns them to read bottom to top
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway

explanation.surface: Most of the capital has been raised as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority of' drops the capital's last letter, and 'raised' reads the rest upwards, as a down entry allows. The capital is Norway's.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean as well or besides, adding something further.

clue.text: Royal house — time for Charlie to show appreciation?

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another, so the C is swapped out

parts.note: a palace is a royal residence
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: At the royal house it is time for Prince Charlie to show his gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time for Charlie' means T replaces C in PALACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A discerning sense of taste, as in a refined palate for wine, is an ability to appreciate.

clue.text: Grass and booze covering food carrier

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other, so these letters go round it

parts.note: beer is a common alcoholic drink
a tray is used for carrying food

explanation.surface: A list of things: some grass, and booze spilled over a tray of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts BE and ER either side of TRAY. 'Grass' is slang for an informer, not the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is an informer who tells on others, which is a kind of traitor.

clue.text: Lie about going to clubs perhaps in smart gear

parts.note: to lounge is to lie about lazily
clubs is one suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Lazing around before heading to nightclubs while dressed smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs perhaps' is the card suit, not nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's matching jacket and trousers for semi-formal daytime wear is smart attire.

clue.text: Drunk guy maybe, pedestrian performer who looks about to drop off?

definitions.text: performer who looks about to drop off?

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a guy rope is one kind of rope, holding a tent down
a pedestrian is someone on foot, a walker

explanation.surface: A drunk man, perhaps a pedestrian, sways like someone about to nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop off' looks like falling asleep but means falling from the high wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus artist balancing on a high wire always seems in danger of falling.

clue.text: Heart-throb's song and dance go wrong, getting upset

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss, an ado

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting letters turns them bottom to top

parts.note: to sin is to go morally wrong

explanation.surface: A pop idol's song-and-dance routine fails and leaves him upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song and dance' is a fuss, not a stage act; 'getting upset' reads the wrongdoing bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikingly handsome young man, named after the youth loved by Aphrodite, is a heart-throb.

clue.text: Twisting in Bengali's net, unusual thing for eating

indicators.note: turning around, so the letters found are read backwards
the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: Something odd for eating gets twisted in a Bengali's net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds LISNETU inside 'Bengali's net, unusual', and 'Twisting' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fork or spoon is an implement used at the table for eating.

clue.text: Had a tramp cooked up drug taken by old rocker?

indicators.note: taken into, so placed inside these letters

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth devoted to rock and roll

indicators.note: something cooked up is invented or rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether a vagrant cooked up drugs that an ageing rocker took.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked up' rearranges the drug; 'taken by' places it inside a Teddy boy, the 1950s British rock-and-roll youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on a tramp is a long weary walk, plodding heavily.

clue.text: Maybe steak-and-kidneys and veg, seconds coming at the end

indicators.note: the letter moves from the front to the back

parts.note: a spud is a potato

explanation.surface: A British dinner of steak-and-kidney and vegetables, with second helpings at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming at the end' moves the S of SPUD to the back. Steak-and-kidney pudding is a classic British savoury suet dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak-and-kidney puddings are examples of British savoury suet puddings, informally shortened.

clue.text: Shattering exercises to unwind

indicators.note: the letters are put through their paces, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Exhausting workouts as a way of winding down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattering' looks like the adjective for exhausting, but is the fodder that 'exercises' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind a coiled cable is to take the kinks out of it and make it even.

clue.text: Cut a plant, they say it's tasty

indicators.note: spoken, so what is heard gives the entry

parts.note: to pick a lily is to cut a plant

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a plant and declares it delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' turns 'pick a lily' into a mustard pickle, a relish served with cold meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This chunky yellow mustard pickle is a flavoursome relish.

clue.text: Check about mother's stay

indicators.note: around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A check on whether mother is staying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the restraint around mother. 'Check' looks like a verb of inspection but means restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to stay behind or continue in the same place.

clue.text: Funds for the old writer, one being housed by offspring

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: lodged within, so one letter sits inside the word

parts.note: sons are offspring
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An elderly writer has money while one of their children puts them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being housed by' lodges the numeral one inside the offspring, all after the writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement income paid regularly to people past working age is what keeps the elderly.

clue.text: Doddering eccentric, pierced and tattooed (head only)

indicators.note: odd and off-centre, so the letters are scrambled
just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An eccentric old man with piercings and only his head tattooed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a description of the doddering person but rearranges PIERCED into DECREPI; 'head only' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worn out and feeble with age totters and shakes as they move.

clue.text: Changed sides and caught foxtrot instead of tango

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: detected means caught or found out
tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ballroom dancer switched partners, caught dancing a foxtrot when a tango was due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foxtrot instead of tango' puts F in place of T in DETECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over to the enemy or a rival party is to switch allegiance.

clue.text: Having forgotten odd bits of Byron, lip-reads, inverting order

indicators.note: turned upside down, so in a down entry the letters run backwards
the odd-placed letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Forgetting bits of Byron, someone lip-reads the poet with the lines in the wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of BYRON LIPREADS give YOLPES, then 'inverting' makes it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To position troops or resources for action is to marshal or arrange them.

clue.text: Straightforward command

explanation.surface: A plain, straightforward order.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and frank describes candid speech; to order someone is to instruct them.

clue.text: Lectures this person's held in markets

indicators.note: kept within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: trades are the markets in which commerce happens
this person is the setter, I, and 's here is 'is'

explanation.surface: The setter gives lectures in the marketplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' puts I inside TRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry speeches of reproach are harangues, scolding lectures.

clue.text: Increased touring to Italy, a paradise

indicators.note: travelling round, so the letters go around the next piece

parts.note: up means raised or increased
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: More people touring Italy, a paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' wraps the word for increased around 'to'; Italy's vehicle code and 'a' follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's ideal imagined island is the model of a perfect place.

clue.text: Recognition of pupil a Tory arranged

indicators.note: pupil and Tory are put in a fresh arrangement, as one arranges flowers, so the letters move

explanation.surface: A Tory organised a pupil's award ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reorders PUPILATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide public acceptance and fame mean being well known and liked.

clue.text: Look after husband's personal growth

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first

parts.note: an air is a manner or appearance

explanation.surface: Advice to look after a husband's self-improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as 'care for', but 'after' places AIR after H. 'Personal growth' is self-improvement on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: What sprouts from a person's scalp is literally the growth on their body.

clue.text: Musical item is set in Washington

indicators.note: a jewel is set in a mount, so these letters are fixed within the other pair

parts.note: DC is short for Washington, District of Columbia

explanation.surface: A musical work is set in America's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in' places 'is' inside the US capital's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A record or CD carries recorded music.

clue.text: Some deliveries friend sent back come together

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler

indicators.note: returned, so read backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Some parcels a friend returned arrive together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some deliveries' is a cricket over, six balls, not parcels; 'sent back' reverses the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: When two things coincide in part, they share space or time.

clue.text: Figure hoarding 1,000 diamonds gets stabbed

indicators.note: holding within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: a price is a figure on a tag
K stands for a thousand
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A figure hoarding a thousand diamonds gets knifed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' puts K in PRICE, and D ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pierced with a sharp point is a light stab.

clue.text: Unfortunately HR miscast comedians — they're employed only once a year

definitions.text: they're employed only once a year

indicators.note: things went wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a card is a joker, a comic person

explanation.surface: Personnel badly cast comedians who only get one booking a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges HRMISCAST into the festival, and comedians are 'cards'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal greetings are sent each December and used only at that festive time.
